decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott and Gholdengo for immediate Prankster Tailwind plus Life Orb Make It Rain pressure, with Gyarados to disrupt rain and Garchomp via Intimidate and Kingambit to punish Gengar, Clefable, and weakened foes with Dark/Steel priority.
decisions.notebook: Primary mode is Whimsicott + Gholdengo Tailwind offense. Gyarados is the preferred rain and Garchomp response; Kingambit supplies Dark pressure and Sucker Punch cleanup. Preserve Whimsicott’s Focus Sash when possible. Hatterene offers a secondary Trick Room mode if the opponent overcommits to speed control or disruption. Passimian is a flexible Fighting-pressure alternative for future games, especially into Steel-heavy positioning.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper leads to set Drizzle + Damp Rock rain, neutering Fire STAB and powering Hurricane/Surf. Clefable (Light Clay) sets 8-turn screens and walls special attackers with Magic Guard.

reflections.summary: Won because Whimsicott established Tailwind while Gholdengo immediately removed Pelipper, then Moonblast and Kingambit's Dark/Steel coverage cleanly answered Garchomp, Mega Gengar, and Clefable. The four brought were broadly appropriate, though Gholdengo was exposed to Mega Gengar's super-effective Shadow Ball; no own Mega Stone holder was available or evolved.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Whimsicott and Kingambit as the safer lead combination, preserve Gholdengo until Mega Gengar is removed, and use Gyarados's Intimidate/Ice Fang as the main Garchomp check rather than relying on a vulnerable early Gholdengo trade.
reflections.notebook: Confirmed Mega Gengar with Shadow Ball, Damp Rock Drizzle Pelipper, Choice Scarf Garchomp locked into Fire Fang after selection, and Light Clay screen-setting Clefable. The opponent can combine rain with fast special pressure and defensive screens. Future plan: prioritize Tailwind plus immediate Dark pressure, avoid exposing Gholdengo before Mega Gengar is handled, and keep Gyarados available for Intimidate and Ice Fang; reassess Hatterene or Passimian only if the opponent changes away from this rain/screen structure.

reflections.summary: Lost because the team had no defensive backbone and the linchpin (Mega Gengar) was KO'd by Kingambit on Turn 2 before it could trap anything. Pelipper died Turn 1 wasting the rain slot (opponent didn't bring Volcarona). Garchomp, Choice-Scarf locked into Fire Fang, missed on Turn 2 — letting Kingambit survive for a free Kowtow Cleave into Gengar. With the trapper gone, Whimsicott's Tailwind-boosted Moonblast and Kingambit's raw power cleaned the remaining two Pokémon (Garchomp then Clefable) on Turn 3. The team preview over-committed to a rain plan and brought four Pokémon that couldn't take a hit from the opponent's Whimsicott/Kingambit core.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Pelipper (dead slot without Volcarona) with a physically bulky Pokémon or a priority user that can outspeed Tailwind. Stop locking Garchomp into a coverage move via Choice Scarf — use a Choice Band or Life Orb set with Earthquake/Stone Edge to threaten Kingambit reliably, or bring a dedicated revenge killer with priority. Ensure at least one team member can survive a Moonblast or Kowtow Cleave and threaten the Whimsicott/Kingambit core.
reflections.notebook: Opponent runs a Whimsicott+Kingambit offensive core with Tailwind support. Whimsicott holds Focus Sash — guaranteed to survive one hit; uses Prankster Tailwind then Moonblast. Kingambit is Adamant/BlackGlasses, runs Kowtow Cleave/Iron Head/Sucker Punch/Protect with Defiant — extremely aggressive, punishes Intimidate and stat drops. Gholdengo (Modest/Life Orb) is a sacrificial special attacker lead. Opponent did NOT bring Volcarona — rain slot (Pelipper+Damp Rock) was wasted. Opponent's 4th slot is one of: Gyarados (Intimidate/Adamant), Passimian (Defiant/Jolly), or Hatterene (Magic Bounce/Quiet). Future plan: drop dedicated rain, bring a bulky pivot or priority user, ensure at least one member walls or threatens the WhimKing core without relying on speed-tied Tailwind races.
